items.question: Which language should the operator speak and answer the call?
items.answer:
According to clause 3.1.1 of the Contact Center division instructions, when answering a
call, the Operator must politely greet and listen carefully in the corresponding language
selected in the IVR menu.

items.question: Should the operator state their surname?
items.answer: If the customer insists, the operator must also provide their surname.

items.question: Should the operator offer additional help at the end of the call?
items.answer:
According to clause 3.1.2 of the Contact Center division instructions, at the end of the
conversation, the operator must clarify whether the customer has any additional
questions. If the customer has no additional questions, it is necessary to thank them for
the call and say goodbye (e.g., "Thank you for your call, goodbye").

items.question: Should they ask if there are additional questions at the end of the call?
items.answer:
According to clause 3.1.2 of the Contact Center division instructions, at the end of the
conversation, the operator must clarify whether the customer has any additional
questions. If the customer has no additional questions, it is necessary to thank them for
the call and say goodbye (e.g., "Thank you for your call, goodbye").

items.question: When should I answer the call?
items.answer:
According to clause 3.2.1 of the Contact Center division instructions, it is desirable to
answer the incoming call after the first ring, and it is mandatory by the third ring.

items.question: What information can be provided to the customer when they call?
items.answer:
According to clause 3.2.2 of the Contact Center division instructions, when a customer
wants to get information about their payment cards and related services, as well as other
bank products, the operator must provide all types of information that do not require
customer identification, do not contradict the Company's internal rules, are covered by the
procedures of the Contact Center division, and do not constitute bank secrecy.

items.question: How should I talk to the customer, and how should I behave?
items.answer:
According to clause 3.2.3 of the Contact Center division instructions, the Operator must
speak politely with the customer, never raise their voice, avoid using unethical words,
refrain from expressing dissatisfaction, mocking, or treating them with criticism. They
should try to assist the applying customer, help eliminate problems related to card usage,
and provide information about instances that can be applied to in any situation. The
Operator must always be attentive to their interlocutor and ensure the provided
information is understood correctly. The tone of voice should be clear and fluent, and they
must speak confidently at a volume the customer can hear. Speech must be rhythmic, and
long pauses should not be allowed.

items.question: Is there a communication standard for speaking with the customer?
items.answer:
According to clause 3.2.3 of the Contact Center division instructions, the Operator must
speak politely with the customer, never raise their voice, avoid using unethical words,
refrain from expressing dissatisfaction, mocking, or treating them with criticism. They
should try to assist the applying customer, help eliminate problems related to card usage,
and provide information about instances that can be applied to in any situation. The
Operator must always be attentive to their interlocutor and ensure the provided
information is understood correctly. The tone of voice should be clear and fluent, and they
must speak confidently at a volume the customer can hear. Speech must be rhythmic, and
long pauses should not be allowed.

items.question: What is identification?
items.answer:
According to clause 4.1.1 of the Contact Center division instructions, identification is the
process of matching the name, surname, full card number, and codeword provided by the
cardholder with the data in the system. To pass identification, the customer must provide
the required information without errors. The execution of requests entering the Customer
Service Department and answering questions related to the card is possible only if the
customer is identified by a codeword or a one-time password replacing the codeword. A
number of exceptions to this process are explained in the Contact Center division
procedure.

items.question: What information is required during identification?
items.answer:
According to the Contact Center division instructions, the name, surname, full card
number, and codeword are required from the customer during identification. This
information is checked by comparing it with the data available in the system. If any of the
information is not provided correctly, the identification is considered unsuccessful, and
the execution of the request becomes impossible.

items.question: Is identification possible without a codeword?
items.answer:
In the absence of a codeword, identification can only be carried out via a one-time
password (OTP) replacing the codeword. The one-time password is sent to the customer's
contact means registered in the system and is valid only for a certain period. If this
password is provided correctly, the customer is considered identified.

items.question: What information can be provided to a customer who fails identification?
items.answer:
No confidential information related to the card or account is provided to a customer who
fails identification. In this case, only general information and procedure rules can be
explained to the customer. Card transactions and answering questions are only possible
after full identification.

items.question: Are there exceptions in the identification process?
items.answer:
Exceptions to the identification process are specifically indicated in the procedure of the
Contact Center division. These exceptions are intended for certain services and special
situations and can only be applied in accordance with the instructions. The operator must
check the relevant procedure requirements before applying exceptional cases.

items.question: How should an operator place a customer on hold?
items.answer:
Before placing a customer on hold, the operator must ask for the customer's permission,
explain exactly why the hold is necessary (e.g., "May I place you on a brief hold while I
check your account history?"), and wait for the customer's affirmative response.

items.question: What is the maximum allowed hold time?
items.answer:
A customer should not be left on hold for more than 2 minutes without an update. If the
issue requires more time, the operator must return to the line, inform the customer of the
delay, and ask if they wish to continue holding or prefer a callback.

items.question: What is the procedure for transferring a call to another department?
items.answer:
The operator must first identify the correct department, inform the customer about the
transfer and the reason for it, and ideally perform a warm transfer by speaking to the
receiving agent to explain the issue before connecting the customer.

items.question: How should an operator handle an abusive or swearing customer?
items.answer:
The operator must remain calm and professional. They should issue a polite warning (e.g.,
"Sir/Madam, I want to help you, but I must ask you to refrain from using inappropriate
language"). If the abuse continues after two warnings, the operator is authorized to
terminate the call after notifying the customer.

items.question: What should be done if a customer reports a lost or stolen card?
items.answer:
The operator must immediately prioritize blocking the card to prevent unauthorized
transactions. Basic identification should be performed swiftly, the card must be blocked in
the system, and the customer should be guided on how to request a replacement.

items.question: How to handle a customer reporting an unrecognized charge?
items.answer:
After fully identifying the customer, the operator should review the transaction details with
them (merchant name, date, amount). If the customer still does not recognize it, the
operator must temporarily block the card to prevent further fraud and guide the customer
through the charge dispute (chargeback) process.

items.question: Can an operator speak to a third party (spouse, parent) about an account?
items.answer:
No confidential account information can be disclosed to a third party unless the primary
account holder is on the line, successfully passes identification, and gives explicit verbal
authorization to the operator to speak with the third party during that specific call.

items.question: What is the procedure when an ATM captures a customer's card?
items.answer:
The operator must identify the customer, block the captured card for security reasons,
inform the customer about the retrieval process (or replacement process, depending on
bank policy), and document the location and ID of the ATM.

items.question: How should an operator respond if the internal banking system goes offline?
items.answer:
The operator must apologize for the technical inconvenience, inform the customer that the
systems are temporarily undergoing maintenance or experiencing an outage, and advise
them to call back after a specified timeframe. No manual workarounds compromising
security should be attempted.

items.question: What steps are required to update a customer's phone number?
items.answer:
Because updating contact information carries high security risks, the operator must
perform strict identification. Often, phone number updates cannot be done via a standard
call and may require the customer to visit a branch or use an authenticated mobile banking
app, depending on the bank's specific security protocol.

items.question: How should an operator handle a dropped call?
items.answer:
If a call drops during an active conversation where the customer was already identified and
an issue was being resolved, the operator should attempt to call the customer back at
least once using the registered phone number.

items.question: What should be done if the customer requests a PIN reset?
items.answer:
Operators generally cannot view or manually reset a PIN. The operator should guide the
customer on how to reset their PIN via secure channels (e.g., mobile banking app, secure
SMS service, or at a designated ATM) after verifying their identity.

items.question: How are VIP or Premium customers handled?
items.answer:
Calls from recognized VIP customers should be routed to a specialized Premium Support
queue if available. If answered by a standard operator, the agent should prioritize the
request, use the appropriate premium greeting, and escalate to a VIP relationship manager
if specialized financial advice is requested.

items.question: What if a customer asks for branch locations and working hours?
items.answer:
This is non-confidential information. The operator does not need to identify the customer
and should promptly provide the nearest branch location, operating hours, and whether
the branch is currently open.

items.question: Can a customer cancel a bank transfer over the phone?
items.answer:
If the transfer is still pending or processing, the operator must identify the customer and
check the system to see if cancellation is technically possible. If the funds have already
cleared and settled into the recipient's account, the transfer cannot be canceled over the
phone, and a formal dispute/recall process must be initiated.

items.question: What should the operator do if they do not speak the customer's language?
items.answer:
The operator should politely inform the customer (using standard phrases if possible) that
they do not speak the language and immediately transfer the call to an agent who speaks
the requested language, or to the appropriate dedicated language queue.

items.question: How is a deceased customer's account handled over the phone?
items.answer:
If a relative calls to report the passing of an account holder, the operator must express
condolences, freeze the account to prevent unauthorized access, and instruct the caller
on the legal documentation (death certificate, inheritance documents) required to be
presented at a physical branch.

items.question: What information is needed to dispute an ATM cash withdrawal error?
items.answer:
The operator must collect the date, time, exact amount attempted, the location/ID of the
ATM, and whether any cash was dispensed at all. The operator will then file a formal
discrepancy ticket for the back-office ATM reconciliation team.

items.question: How should operators handle complaints about bank staff?
items.answer:
The operator must listen empathetically without taking a defensive stance, collect specific
details (branch location, staff name/description, date, and nature of the incident), and log
a formal complaint ticket to be reviewed by the branch management or HR department.

items.question: What should an operator do if a customer requests financial or investment advice?
items.answer:
Call center operators are typically not licensed financial advisors. The operator must
politely explain that they cannot provide direct financial advice and offer to schedule an
appointment with a certified financial advisor or relationship manager at a branch.
